model_annotations.Bulgarian: This bar chart illustrates the relationship between sparsity rate and perplexity for two different configurations, Per-Output and Per-Layer. The horizontal axis, labeled "Sparsity Rate," displays categories ranging from 10% to 80% in 10% increments. The vertical axis, labeled "Perplexity," is on a logarithmic scale with a base of 10, ranging from 10⁰ (approximately 1) to 10² (approximately 100), with tick labels at 10⁰, 10¹, and 10². Two sets of bars are presented, one in blue representing "Per-Output" and the other in orange representing "Per-Layer." The bars are arranged side-by-side for each sparsity rate category, allowing for visual comparison between the two configurations. The shortest blue bar, corresponding to a sparsity rate of 10%, has an approximate value of 1.5, while the tallest blue bar, at 80% sparsity, has an approximate value of 70. The shortest orange bar, at 10% sparsity, has an approximate value of 2, and the tallest orange bar, at 80% sparsity, has an approximate value of 90. The bars are sorted in ascending order based on the sparsity rate, and no bars are visually emphasized beyond their color differentiation.
